about: Facts generate.py can't read from package metadata. Each is pinned to a file and its SHA-256, or to an exact crate version, so a dependency bump that changes one fails generation until someone reviews it again. 'why' says how each was established.

Apache-2.0.why: The canonical Apache License 2.0, given once for every Apache-2.0 Android library (their packages carry no licence file of their own).

arti-MIT.why: Arti's LICENSE-MIT (Copyright 2019-2025, The Tor Project, Inc.) at the commit its crates were published from.

asn1-rs-MIT.why: asn1-rs's LICENSE-MIT at the commit asn1-rs-impl 0.2.0 was published from.

cookie-factory-MIT.why: cookie-factory's REUSE licence file LICENSES/MIT.txt (its .reuse/dep5 names it for every file) at the commit 0.3.3 was published from.

dart-sys-MIT.why: dart-sys's LICENSE-MIT.md at the commit dart-sys 4.1.5 was published from.

derive-deftly-MIT.why: derive-deftly's LICENCE at the commit derive-deftly-macros 1.14.0 was published from.

desugar_jdk_libs.why: GPL-2.0 with the Classpath Exception, as in OpenJDK: the LICENSE of google/desugar_jdk_libs at 50d9c1fb ('Prepare for jdk-11 based desugared library version 2.1.4', 2024-12-18), unchanged since af7193bb (2023-09-27). Its POM names the same licence.

flutter_rust_bridge-MIT.why: flutter_rust_bridge's LICENSE at the commit its 2.11.1 crates were published from.

jitterentropy-LICENSE.why: The Jitter Entropy library's LICENSE at its v3.6.3 release commit (tag v3.6.3 -> c90ff465), the version AWS-LC vendors in aws-lc/third_party/jitterentropy (JENT_MAJVERSION 3, MINVERSION 6, PATCHLEVEL 3). aws-lc-sys's package doesn't include it; its sources say "License: see LICENSE file in root directory". BSD-3-Clause, with a GPL-2.0 alternative that AWS-LC declines; Copyright (C) 2017 - 2025, Stephan Mueller.

jni-sys-MIT.why: jni-sys's LICENSE-MIT at the commit jni-sys-macros 0.4.1 was published from.

material-icons.why: MaterialIcons_LICENSE.txt from Flutter's material_fonts artifact (bin/internal/material_fonts.version), which Flutter installs as bin/cache/artifacts/material_fonts/: the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence. generate.py also compares it with the Flutter SDK's copy on every run.

objc2-licence.why: objc2's LICENSE.md (how its crates are licensed, and its note on Apple SDKs) at the commit its 0.3.2 framework crates were published from.

protobuf.why: Protocol Buffers' BSD-3-Clause licence (Copyright 2008 Google Inc.) at v32.1, the release tink-java v1.19.0 builds with (protobuf-javalite 4.32.1 in its MODULE.bazel). The same text has covered protobuf-java for years.

r8.why: The LICENSE file inside desugar_jdk_libs_configuration 2.1.4's jar (BSD-3-Clause, Copyright (c) 2016, the R8 project authors), as its POM's BSD-3-Clause names.

rust-MIT.why: rust-lang/rust's LICENSE-MIT at tag 1.100.0 (Copyright (c) The Rust Project Contributors).

upstream_licence_files.why: Arti's crates are published without a licence file. Every one of them in the graph names this commit in its .cargo_vcs_info.json. When the fork moves to another Arti release, fetch LICENSE-MIT at the new commit, then update the commit, the file and its sha256.
asn1-rs-impl 0.2.0's package has no licence file.
dart-sys 4.1.5's package has no licence file.
flutter_rust_bridge and flutter_rust_bridge_macros 2.11.1 have no licence file in their packages.
jni 0.22.4's package has no licence file.
jni-macros 0.22.4's package has no licence file.
jni-sys-macros 0.4.1's package has no licence file.
objc2-core-foundation and objc2-io-kit 0.3.2 ship no licence file, and objc2's repository has no MIT file with a copyright line: its LICENSE.md is shipped as a notice, with the standard MIT text.
derive-deftly-macros 1.14.0's package has no licence file.
cookie-factory 0.3.3's package has no licence file.

no_licence_file.amplify_num 0.5.4: Checked: no licence file in the package; its repository's LICENSE (amplify-num at 872842c3) is the bare Apache License text with no copyright line, which is what the standard text gives.
no_licence_file.amplify_syn 2.0.1: Checked: no licence file in the package; its repository's LICENSE (amplify-derive at 29ca86c5) is the bare Apache License text with no copyright line.
no_licence_file.void 1.0.2: Checked: no licence file in the package, which records no publishing commit, and none in reem/rust-void at its 1.0.2 tag (ab2f4dbb); a LICENSE-MIT was added there later.

dunce 1.0.5.why: `CC0-1.0 OR MIT-0 OR Apache-2.0`; the package's only licence file is the CC0 1.0 Universal text. cargo-about prefers Apache-2.0 (earlier in `accepted`), which the package has no text for, so the option it does ship is used. A build dependency of aws-lc-sys (Windows path handling in its build script).

amplify_num 0.5.4.end:
// Copyright (C) 2020-2026 Dr Maxim Orlovsky.
// All rights reserved.
amplify_num 0.5.4.why: The package ships no licence file and its repository's LICENSE is the bare Apache text, but src/lib.rs's header carries its copyright lines.

ident_case 1.0.1.why: Its licence files name no copyright holder; src/lib.rs's header does.

sync_wrapper 1.0.2.why: Its LICENSE is the Apache text with the appendix unfilled; src/lib.rs's header carries the copyright line.

amplify_syn 2.0.1.why: For consistency with amplify_num: the authorship line of its src/lib.rs header. (The header then dedicates the code to the public domain and points to MIT, while Cargo.toml says Apache-2.0; the notices follow Cargo.toml.)

LICENSE-THIRD-PARTY.summary: its notices cover examples and tests, which aren't compiled
LICENSE-THIRD-PARTY.why: Its parts are for files the library doesn't compile: matching.go (CC BY 3.0) for examples/matching.rs, the Go Programming Language (BSD-3-Clause) for tests/golang.rs, and the Rust Programming Language (MIT OR Apache-2.0) for tests/mpsc.rs; src/ names none of them.

xz/COPYING.summary: XZ Utils' licence summary; the compiled liblzma is 0BSD, shipped
xz/COPYING.why: XZ Utils' summary of its licences. build.rs compiles only xz/src/liblzma and xz/src/common (tuklib), both 0BSD: xz/COPYING.0BSD ships as the bundled source's licence, with the notice line this file suggests.

xz/COPYING.GPLv2.summary: covers XZ Utils' scripts, not compiled
xz/COPYING.GPLv2.why: For XZ Utils' scripts (xzgrep and others) and build system, which aren't compiled.

xz/COPYING.GPLv3.summary: covers XZ Utils' build system, not compiled
xz/COPYING.GPLv3.why: For parts of XZ Utils' build system, not compiled.

xz/COPYING.LGPLv2.1.summary: covers getopt for XZ Utils' tools, not compiled
xz/COPYING.LGPLv2.1.why: For the getopt_long the xz command-line tools may link; the tools aren't compiled.

xz/build-aux/license-check.sh.why: A maintainer script that checks XZ Utils' file licences; not a licence, not compiled.

sqlcipher/LICENSE.summary: SQLCipher's licence; SQLCipher is built only with features that are off
sqlcipher/LICENSE.why: SQLCipher's BSD-style licence (Zetetic LLC), for the bundled SQLCipher amalgamation, which build.rs compiles only with the `sqlcipher` or `bundled-sqlcipher` features. Generation checks with cargo tree that none is on; the plain SQLite amalgamation is what's built (its notice ships under bundled_sources).

LICENSE.md.summary: its Go Authors notice covers code only the off `compact` feature compiles
LICENSE.md.why: Beyond pointing to LICENSE-MIT/LICENSE-APACHE, it carries the Go Authors' BSD-3-Clause notice for src/bellerophon.rs, which only the `compact` feature compiles. Generation checks with cargo tree that `compact` is off on every target.

LICENSE-THIRD-PARTY.why: Copyright 2014-2020 The Rust Project Developers, Apache-2.0 OR MIT, for code derived from the Rust standard library. Shipped as parking's notice: the standard library entry's text is the same licence, but this is the copyright line for the code parking compiles.

src/unicode_tables/LICENSE-UNICODE.why: The Unicode licence for the data in src/unicode_tables/. Of the `unicode-*` features, cargo tree shows only `unicode-case` on (with `std`) for all four targets; it compiles case_folding_simple.rs, Unicode data under this licence, which asks that its notice appear with all copies. That is why it ships.

src/spin/LICENSE.why: MIT, Copyright (c) 2014 Mathijs van de Nes, for the vendored copy of spin in src/spin/. It is not compiled: lib.rs declares the module only under #[cfg(not(feature = "std"))], and cargo tree shows `std` on for all four targets. Shipped by review even so (cargo-about also reads it as one of the crate's licence files).

zstd/COPYING.summary: the GPL-2.0 option of Zstandard's dual licence; BSD-3-Clause is the one used
zstd/COPYING.why: The GPL-2.0 text of Zstandard's `BSD-3-Clause OR GPL-2.0-only` licence. The BSD-3-Clause option is chosen, and zstd/LICENSE ships as the bundled source's licence.

bundled_sources.name: AWS-LC
bundled_sources.license: ISC AND Apache-2.0 AND MIT AND BSD-3-Clause
bundled_sources.expression: ISC AND (Apache-2.0 OR ISC) AND Apache-2.0 AND MIT AND BSD-3-Clause AND (Apache-2.0 OR ISC OR MIT) AND (Apache-2.0 OR ISC OR MIT-0)

extra.why: fiat-crypto's MIT licence (Copyright (c) 2015-2020 the fiat-crypto authors), the only third-party licence file in the package. Its generated field arithmetic (third_party/fiat/*.h) is compiled on every target.

The Jitter Entropy RNG (third_party/jitterentropy, v3.6.3) is compiled on Android and, when the SDK has CoreServices, on iOS (builder/main.rs should_build_jitter_entropy). Its sources point to a LICENSE the package leaves out, so the upstream file at v3.6.3 ships, used under its BSD option as AWS-LC elects. That file names Stephan Mueller; two source files also name Joshua E. Hill, whose line is prepended.

bundled_sources.why: aws-lc-sys's cc builder ("Building with: CC"; AWS_LC_SYS_USE_SYSTEM=0, which the fork's cargokit sets, forbids a system AWS-LC) compiles AWS-LC 5.12.0 (include/openssl/base.h AWSLC_VERSION_NUMBER_STRING) from aws-lc/crypto, generated-src and third_party on all four targets. aws-lc/LICENSE (the crate's own LICENSE has the same text, bar one trailing space) covers it: new AWS-LC code Apache-2.0 OR ISC, BoringSSL-derived ISC or Apache-2.0, OpenSSL-derived Apache-2.0 (no OpenSSL or SSLeay licence text remains since AWS-LC's 2026 relicensing), mlkem-native and mldsa-native Apache-2.0 OR ISC OR MIT, s2n-bignum Apache-2.0 OR ISC OR MIT-0 (its LICENSE is not in the package; its copyright line and those texts are in aws-lc/LICENSE), public-domain (CC0) Keccak and AES reference code. The SPDX lines of the compiled sources are exactly those (crypto: Apache-2.0, ISC, Apache-2.0 OR ISC, Apache-2.0 OR ISC OR MIT; third_party: the same plus Apache-2.0 OR ISC OR MIT-0); the files without one are perlasm output, fiat-crypto's and jitterentropy's, listed below. Used under ISC where ISC is offered.

bundled_sources.name: SQLite
bundled_sources.start: ** The author disclaims copyright to this source code.
bundled_sources.end: May you share freely, never taking more than you give.
bundled_sources.why: The `bundled` feature compiles this amalgamation (SQLITE_VERSION 3.53.2) on both platforms. SQLite is in the public domain; this is its own notice.

bundled_sources.name: XZ Utils (liblzma)
bundled_sources.notice: Copyright (C) The XZ Utils authors and contributors
bundled_sources.why: The `static` feature compiles xz/src/liblzma and xz/src/common (tuklib), both 0BSD per xz/COPYING; the notice line is the one xz/COPYING suggests.

bundled_sources.name: Zstandard
bundled_sources.why: Without its pkg-config feature, zstd-sys compiles the bundled zstd/lib/common, compress and decompress. Zstandard is dual-licensed; BSD-3-Clause is chosen. Two default features would compile sources under other licences: `zdict_builder` (zstd/lib/dictBuilder, whose divsufsort.c is MIT, Copyright (c) 2003-2008 Yuta Mori, in its source header only) and `legacy` (zstd/lib/legacy, whose old-format decoders carry BSD-2-Clause blocks). They are off because zstd-safe depends on zstd-sys without default features and no crate turns them back on; generation checks with cargo tree that both stay off on every target. The Rust crates around it were relicensed with zstd 0.14 / zstd-safe 8.3 / zstd-sys 2.1: zstd and zstd-safe from MIT (OR Apache-2.0) to BSD-3-Clause (Copyright (c) 2026, Alexandre Bury), and zstd-sys to `BSD-3-Clause AND BSD-2-Clause`, its LICENSE.BSD-3-Clause for the generated bindings and LICENSE.BSD-2-Clause for the legacy decoders (compiled only with `legacy`, which is off; the text ships anyway, as the crate's own expression requires it). zstd-sys 2.1's build.rs keeps the same cc source list; its new `cmake` (same sources), `rust-backend` (libzstd-rs-sys instead of C) and `pkg-config`/`vendored` switches are off.

bundled_sources.name: Dart SDK (dart_api_dl)
bundled_sources.why: build.rs compiles the Dart SDK's dart_api_dl.c (dart-sdk/include, version 3.2.3) into the library.

native_code_reviewed.aws-lc-rs: Declares `links` but compiles no C of its own (the package has no C sources): build.rs only reads environment variables and re-exports aws-lc-sys's DEP_AWS_LC_* values. The AWS-LC it links is aws-lc-sys's, listed under bundled_sources.
native_code_reviewed.oslog: build.rs compiles the crate's own wrapper.c, covered by the crate's MIT licence.

androidx.datastore:datastore-preferences.why: Its POM: 'Repackaged proto-lite dependency for use by datastore preferences', BSD-3-Clause.

androidx.glance:glance-appwidget-externa.why: Its POM: a repackaged proto-lite for Glance, BSD-3-Clause.

com.android.tools:desugar_jdk_libs_confi.why: desugar_jdk_libs depends on it; its jar holds the conversion classes D8 adds alongside the desugared library.

com.android.tools:desugar_jdk_libs.why: Core library desugaring (the app's coreLibraryDesugaring): D8/L8 compile the parts the app uses into the APK. GPL-2.0 is copyleft: its source, at the 2.1.4 release commit, is linked as with the MPL crates.

maven_embedded.name: Protocol Buffers (protobuf-javalite 4.32.1, shaded into tink-android)
maven_embedded.why: tink-android 1.19.0's jar holds 543 classes under com/google/crypto/tink/shaded/protobuf/ and its POM declares no protobuf dependency (checked by listing the jar from Maven Central).

LicenseRef-Android-SDK-License.name: Android Software Development Kit License Agreement

LicenseRef-Play-Core-SDK-Terms.name: Play Core Software Development Kit Terms of Service

toolchain.name: Rust standard library
toolchain.note: Linked into Bag's Tor library on every target. The standard library's own third-party components are listed in COPYRIGHT-library.html, shipped with the Rust toolchain (share/doc/rust/).
toolchain.why: std, core and alloc are statically linked into librust_lib_tor. The version is the fork's rust/rust-toolchain, which generate.py checks, and the release workflow's RUST_TOOLCHAIN, which its own check ties to this entry.

MaterialIcons.name: Material Icons font
MaterialIcons.notice: © Google. Release builds carry a modified copy: Flutter's icon tree shaking keeps only the glyphs Bag uses
MaterialIcons.why: pubspec.yaml's `uses-material-design: true` makes Flutter bundle fonts/MaterialIcons-Regular.otf (tree-shaken to the icons the app uses) in every build, under the licence Flutter ships with it. Neither flutter_tools' NOTICES nor sky_engine's LICENSE carries that notice, so it would otherwise be missing.
